title_en: Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Improving the Working Mechanism of the Judicial Committees of People's Courts
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Opinions on Improving and Perfecting the Working Mechanism of the Judicial Committee of People's Courts

Fa Fa [2019] No. 20

In order to implement the Central Government's overall deployment on deepening the comprehensive and coordinated reform of the judicial system, improve and perfect the working mechanism of the Judicial Committee of people's courts, and further fully implement the judicial accountability system, these Opinions are formulated in accordance with the Organic Law of the People's Courts, the Criminal Procedure Law, the Civil Procedure Law, the Administrative Procedure Law, and other laws and judicial interpretations, and in light of the actual work of people's courts.

I. Basic Principles

1. Uphold the leadership of the Party. Adhere to the guidance of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, strengthen the "Four Consciousnesses," firm up the "Four Confidences," and achieve the "Two Upholds." Uphold the absolute leadership of the Party over the work of people's courts, unswervingly follow the path of socialist rule of law with Chinese characteristics, and improve a fair, efficient, and authoritative socialist judicial system.

2. Practice democratic centralism. Adhere to the organic combination of fully developing democracy and correctly exercising centralism. Improve and perfect the议事 rules and议事 procedures of the Judicial Committee, ensure that members of the Judicial Committee express their opinions objectively, fairly, independently, and equally, prevent and overcome situations of endless discussion without decision and decisions without implementation, and effectively leverage the advantages of democratic centralism.

3. Follow the laws of judicial work. Optimize the composition of the Judicial Committee, scientifically define the functions of the Judicial Committee, improve the operating mechanism of the Judicial Committee, fully implement the judicial accountability system, and promote the establishment of a working mechanism with clear powers and responsibilities, unified powers and responsibilities, efficient operation, and strong supervision.

4. Abide by judicial fairness. Carefully summarize the experience of reforming the Judicial Committee system, continuously improve the working mechanism, adhere to the facts as the basis and the law as the criterion, adhere to strict and impartial justice, adhere to the unity of procedural justice and substantive justice, give full play to the functional role of the Judicial Committee, and strive to make the people feel fairness and justice in every judicial case.

II. Organizational Composition

5. People's courts at all levels shall establish a Judicial Committee. The Judicial Committee shall be composed of the President, Vice Presidents, and a number of senior judges, and the number of its members shall be an odd number. The Judicial Committee may have full-time members.

6. Meetings of the Judicial Committee are divided into plenary meetings and specialized committee meetings. Specialized committee meetings are a form of meeting and a working method of the Judicial Committee. Intermediate People's Courts and above may, based on the needs of trial work, convene specialized committee meetings for criminal trials, civil and administrative trials, etc. The composition of specialized committee meetings shall be determined based on the expertise and work division of the members of the Judicial Committee. Members of the Judicial Committee may participate in different specialized committee meetings. The total number of members of all specialized committee meetings shall exceed one-half of the total number of members of the Judicial Committee.

III. Functional Positioning

7. The main functions of the Judicial Committee are:
(1) Summarizing trial work experience;
(2) Discussing and deciding on the application of law in major, difficult, and complex cases;
(3) Discussing and deciding whether judgments, rulings, and mediation statements that have already taken legal effect rendered by this court should be retried;
(4) Discussing and deciding other major issues concerning trial work. The Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court unifies the application of law by formulating judicial interpretations, normative documents, and issuing guiding cases.

8. The following cases tried by people's courts at all levels shall be submitted to the Judicial Committee for discussion and decision:
(1) Sensitive cases involving national security, foreign affairs, social stability, etc., and major, difficult, and complex cases;
(2) Cases where judgments, rulings, and mediation statements that have already taken legal effect rendered by this court are indeed erroneous and need retrial;
(3) Criminal cases where the People's Procuratorate at the same level protests in accordance with the procedure for trial supervision;
(4) New types of cases where the rules for application of law are unclear;
(5) Cases where the defendant is proposed to be acquitted;
(6) Cases where the proposed sentence is below the statutory punishment or where the defendant is exempted from criminal punishment; cases where a High People's Court or an Intermediate People's Court proposes to impose a death sentence shall be submitted to the Judicial Committee of that court for discussion and decision.

9. The following cases tried by people's courts at all levels may be submitted to the Judicial Committee for discussion and decision:
(1) Cases where the Collegial Panel has significant divergent opinions on the application of law, and it is difficult to reach a decision after discussion at the Professional (Presiding) Judges' Meeting;
(2) Cases where the proposed judgment may conflict with similar cases previously adjudicated by this court or a higher court;
(3) Major, difficult, and complex civil cases and administrative cases where the People's Procuratorate at the same level protests in accordance with the procedure for trial supervision;
(4) Cases where a retrial is ordered or the case is remanded for retrial;
(5) Other cases that need to be submitted to the Judicial Committee for discussion and decision.

IV. Operational Mechanism

10. If a Collegial Panel or a Sole Judge believes that a case needs to be submitted to the Judicial Committee for discussion and decision, they shall file an application and report it level by level for approval by the President. If no application is filed but the President deems it necessary, the President may refer the matter to the Judicial Committee for discussion and decision. The submission of other matters to the Judicial Committee for discussion and decision shall follow the procedures applicable to case submission mutatis mutandis.

11. Cases proposed to be submitted to the Judicial Committee for discussion and decision shall have the opinions from the research and discussion of the Professional (Presiding) Judges' Meeting. If the opinions of the Professional (Presiding) Judges' Meeting are inconsistent with the opinions of the Collegial Panel or Sole Judge, the President, Vice President, or Division Chief may, in accordance with trial supervision and management authority, require the Collegial Panel or Sole Judge to reconsider; if the opinions of the Professional (Presiding) Judges' Meeting are still not adopted after reconsideration, the matter shall be reported to the Judicial Committee for discussion and decision in accordance with the procedures.

12. For cases submitted to the Judicial Committee for discussion, the Collegial Panel shall prepare a written report. The written report shall objectively and comprehensively reflect the facts of the case, evidence, opinions of the parties or the prosecution and defense, list the issues of application of law that need to be decided by the Judicial Committee, the opinions of the Professional (Presiding) Judges' Meeting, the results of the search for similar cases and related cases, and include the proposed handling opinion and reasons of the Collegial Panel. If there are divergent opinions, the different opinions and reasons shall be summarized.

Before other matters are submitted to the Judicial Committee for discussion, the responsible department shall, on the basis of careful research and consultation with relevant departments, propose handling opinions.

13. For cases or matters submitted to the Judicial Committee for discussion and decision, the working department of the Judicial Committee may first review whether they fall within the scope of discussion of the Judicial Committee and propose opinions, and report to the President for decision.

14. For cases submitted to the Judicial Committee for discussion and decision, if a member of the Judicial Committee has circumstances requiring recusal, they shall voluntarily recuse themselves and report to the President for decision; the recusal of the President shall be decided by the Judicial Committee. The circumstances for recusal of members of the Judicial Committee shall be governed by the relevant legal provisions concerning the recusal of judicial personnel.

15. Members of the Judicial Committee shall review the meeting materials in advance, and if necessary, may review the relevant case files, documents, and audio and video materials of court hearings.

16. When the Judicial Committee holds plenary meetings or specialized committee meetings, more than half of its members shall be present.

17. Plenary meetings and specialized committee meetings of the Judicial Committee shall be presided over by the President or a Vice President authorized by the President.

18. The following persons shall attend the meetings of the Judicial Committee as non-voting participants:
(1) The members of the Collegial Panel handling the case, the Sole Judge, or the person handling the matter;
(2) The head of the trial division or department handling the case or matter;
(3) Other persons whose attendance is deemed necessary. When the Judicial Committee holds a meeting, it may, if necessary, invite deputies to the People's Congress, members of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, experts, scholars, etc. to attend as non-voting participants. With the consent of the presiding officer, non-voting participants may provide explanations or express opinions, but shall not participate in the voting.

19. When the Judicial Committee holds a meeting, the Procurator-General of the People's Procuratorate at the same level, or a Deputy Procurator-General authorized by them, may attend as a non-voting participant.

20. When the Judicial Committee discusses and decides on cases and matters, it generally follows the following procedures:
(1) Report by the Collegial Panel or the person handling the matter;
(2) Questions from members on relevant issues;
(3) Members express opinions in order from lower to higher judicial rank and seniority, with the presiding officer expressing opinions last;
(4) The presiding officer summarizes the meeting, and the meeting makes a resolution.

21. When the plenary meetings or specialized committee meetings of the Judicial Committee discuss cases or matters, decisions are generally made by a majority opinion of more than half of all their respective members, and the opinions of the minority members shall be recorded.

If a case or matter discussed at a specialized committee meeting cannot form a resolution, or if the President deems it necessary, it may be submitted to the plenary meeting for discussion and decision.

If the President deems it necessary regarding a case or matter discussed at a plenary meeting or specialized committee meeting of the Judicial Committee, the President may request reconsideration.

22. The Collegial Panel, Sole Judge, or relevant departments shall implement the decisions made by the Judicial Committee after discussing cases or matters. If the working department of the Judicial Committee finds that the handling result of a case does not conform to the decision of the Judicial Committee, it shall promptly report to the President.

23. The meeting minutes or decisions of the Judicial Committee, after being reviewed and approved by the President, shall be distributed to the members of the Judicial Committee and the relevant trial divisions or departments.

If the Procurator-General or Deputy Procurator-General of the People's Procuratorate at the same level attended the Judicial Committee meeting as a non-voting participant, the meeting minutes or decisions shall be copied to the working body of the Procuratorial Committee of that People's Procuratorate.

24. The decisions of the Judicial Committee on cases discussed and their reasons shall be disclosed in the judgment documents, unless otherwise provided by law for non-disclosure.

25. For cases decided upon by the Judicial Committee, the Collegial Panel or Sole Judge shall promptly conclude the case and submit the judgment, ruling, mediation statement, etc., to the working department of the Judicial Committee for filing.

26. People's courts at all levels shall establish a system of audio and video recording of the entire Judicial Committee meeting, managed in accordance with confidentiality requirements. The submission, review, discussion, and decision of topics for the Judicial Committee shall be integrated into the trial process management system, with full documentation.

27. The working department of the Judicial Committee in people's courts at all levels shall be responsible for handling the daily administrative work of the Judicial Committee, supervising and inspecting the implementation of decisions of the Judicial Committee as authorized by the Judicial Committee, and implementing other matters assigned by the Judicial Committee.

V. Guarantee and Supervision

28. The lawful performance of duties by members of the Judicial Committee is protected by law.

29. If leading cadres or internal personnel of judicial organs illegally interfere, inquire about, or meddle in cases discussed and decided by members of the Judicial Committee, such conduct shall be recorded, reported, and corresponding responsibility shall be pursued in accordance with discipline and law.

30. If members of the Judicial Committee suffer false accusations, framing, insults, or slander due to their lawful performance of duties, the people's court shall, together with relevant departments, promptly take effective measures to clarify the facts, eliminate adverse effects, and pursue the responsibility of the relevant unit or individual in accordance with the law.

31. When the Judicial Committee discusses cases, the Collegial Panel or Sole Judge is responsible for the facts they report, and the members of the Judicial Committee are responsible for the opinions they express and their votes.

32. If members of the Judicial Committee commit serious violations of discipline or law such as embezzlement or bribery, engaging in malpractice for personal gain, or rendering judgments that pervert the law, they shall be seriously held accountable in accordance with discipline and law.

33. People's courts at all levels shall include the attendance rate of members of the Judicial Committee at meetings in the assessment system and publicly disclose it within the court in an appropriate manner.

34. Members of the Judicial Committee, non-voting participants, and other meeting attendees shall strictly abide by the work discipline of confidentiality and shall not disclose the secrets of trial work learned in the course of performing their duties. If disclosure causes serious consequences, disciplinary and legal responsibility shall be strictly pursued.

VI. Supplementary Provisions

35. The scope of trial responsibility of members of the Judicial Committee, its determination, and accountability procedures as referred to in these Opinions shall be implemented in accordance with the "Several Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Improving the Judicial Accountability System of People's Courts" and relevant provisions on judge discipline.

36. People's courts at all levels may, in accordance with these Opinions and in light of the actual trial work of their own courts, formulate implementation rules.

37. These Opinions shall come into force on August 2, 2019. If any normative documents previously issued by the Supreme People's Court are inconsistent with these Opinions, these Opinions shall prevail.

August 2, 2019
